verbalization: Nisoldipine, a dihydropyridine, is linked to Cacna1d through a series of molecular interactions that involve calcium channel modulation. The evidence suggests that Nisoldipine, as part of the dihydropyridine class, binds to calcium channels, which are targeted by Felodipine, a closely related dihydropyridine. This binding is mediated through the lowest common ancestor of Nisoldipine and Felodipine, which is the dihydropyridine class. The relationship between Nisoldipine and Cacna1d is thus inferred through the shared mechanism of calcium channel blockade, which is a well-established pharmacological property of dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers. The integration of these pathways highlights the role of calcium channels in the pharmacological action of Nisoldipine, with Cacna1d being a key target in this process.
